title: Suvendu Adhikari promises tribal university in Jhargram, forest land titles for more villages
dek: On Janajatiya Gaurav Diwas, the chief minister launched 188 projects in Jhargram district and said the hospital there would become a super-speciality facility.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Sunday that the state would set up a tribal university in Jhargram and upgrade the district hospital to a super-speciality hospital, at a Janajatiya Gaurav Diwas event marking the 151st birth anniversary of the tribal leader Birsa Munda, according to reports.

He laid foundation stones for 137 projects worth Rs 274.43 crore and opened 51 completed projects worth Rs 47.59 crore in the district. He said 770 tribal beneficiaries had received forest land titles and that data had been collected from 1,237 forest villages so that more titles could be given. All eligible folk artistes would be brought under the state's Lokprasar Shilpi allowance scheme by 31 December, he said, and a rise in the allowance would be considered in the next state Budget. Eligible members of the Sabar community, one of the state's particularly vulnerable tribal groups, would get benefits under state-funded schemes.

Mr Adhikari blamed the previous Trinamool Congress government for irregularities in the issue of Scheduled Tribe certificates and said 73 people had been held for allegedly obtaining certificates by falsely claiming tribal identity; the figure was his and was not independently confirmed. No response from the Trinamool had been reported by Monday evening. Jhargram is part of the Jangalmahal region of western Bengal, where tribal communities make up a large part of the population.

sources.title: Millennium Post: CM promises tribal university, land rights push in Junglemahal
